title: Closed residue algebraicity over a local ring of dimension at most one
statement: Let $(B,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring, meaning a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and assume $\dim B\leq1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $C$ be a commutative finite type $B$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. For a prime ideal $T$ in a ring $H$, write $\kappa(T)=\operatorname{Frac}(H/T)$, the residue field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; a minimal prime is a prime containing no strictly smaller prime. Suppose that for every minimal prime $Q\subset C$, with contraction $q\subset B$, the induced field extension $\kappa(q)\subseteq\kappa(Q)$ is algebraic, meaning that every element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $\kappa(q)$. Then every prime $P\subset C$ with $P\cap B=\mathfrak m$ satisfies $\operatorname{trdeg}_{B/\mathfrak m}\kappa(P)=0$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. The assertion allows nonreduced $B$ and $C$, zero-dimensional $B$, vertical components whose generic prime contracts to $\mathfrak m$, and an empty closed fibre.

source.place: Tag 0AB6, label lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1, proof of condition (2), reduced-component and vertical/horizontal dimension-inequality paragraphs (returned proof steps 5–7).

proof.text: Fix a prime $P$ over $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime], choose a minimal prime $Q\subseteq P$ of $C$. Put $q=Q\cap B$, $R=B/q$, $D=C/Q$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m/q$, and $p=P/Q$. The induced map $R\hookrightarrow D$ is injective between domains, and $p\cap R=\mathfrak n$. Quotient ideals correspond by inverse image: primality follows from the test $ab\in I$, and inclusions are preserved. Each ideal of $R$ is generated by images of generators of its inverse image in $B$, so $R$ is Noetherian. Images of algebra generators of $C$ generate $D$ over $R$. Moreover $R$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$. The equality $D/p=C/P$ identifies $\kappa(p)=\kappa(P)$ over $R/\mathfrak n=B/\mathfrak m$. By hypothesis $\operatorname{Frac}(D)=\kappa(Q)$ is algebraic over $\operatorname{Frac}(R)=\kappa(q)$.

source.place: Tag 0AB6, label lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1, proof of (2), reduction to reduced components and the vertical/horizontal cases.

proof.text: If $q=\mathfrak m$, then $R=B/\mathfrak m$ is a field. Every nonzero $d\in D$ satisfies a relation $a_0+a_1d+\cdots+a_nd^n=0$ with $a_0\ne0$: remove powers of $T$ from any nonzero annihilating polynomial, using that $d\ne0$ in a domain. Thus $d^{-1}=-a_0^{-1}(a_1+\cdots+a_nd^{n-1})\in D$. Hence $D$ is a field, $p=0$, and $\kappa(P)=D$ is algebraic over $B/\mathfrak m$. Every singleton is algebraically dependent, so the definition of transcendence degree gives the required value zero.

source.place: Tag 0AB6, label lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1, proof of (2), reduction to reduced components and the vertical/horizontal cases.

proof.text: Suppose $q\ne\mathfrak m$. The strict prime chain $q\subsetneq\mathfrak m$ and $\dim B\le1$ show that no prime lies strictly below $q$. Prime chains in $R$ lift to chains in $B$, so $\dim R\le1$. The strict chain $0\subsetneq\mathfrak n$ shows that $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak n)=1$. Also $p\ne0$, since its contraction is the nonzero ideal $\mathfrak n$; the chain $0\subsetneq p$ in the domain $D$ gives $\operatorname{ht}(p)\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 0AB6, label lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1, proof of (2), reduction to reduced components and the vertical/horizontal cases.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-dimension-inequality] to $R\subset D$, $\mathfrak n$, and $p$. Step 1 supplies Noetherianity, finite type, domains, injectivity and the contraction condition. Its generic transcendence term $\operatorname{trdeg}_R D$ is zero: for each $d\in D$ clear denominators in a nonzero annihilating polynomial over $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ to obtain a nonzero polynomial over $R$. Thus no singleton in $D$ is algebraically independent. Writing $t=\operatorname{trdeg}_{R/\mathfrak n}\kappa(p)$, the cited inequality gives $1\le\operatorname{ht}(p)\le1-t$. Consequently $t=0$. Step 1 identifies this with the asserted transcendence degree for $P$. The choice of $P$ was arbitrary; if no such prime exists, the assertion is vacuous.
